title: The Spine
question: Which part of the spine is it?
lines: Seven small bones hold up your head. Which part of the spine?
Watch the glowing section at the top of the spine.
Which part of the spine is glowing?
The lumbar section is the low back, with larger bones.
The seven glowing vertebrae are in the neck.
It's B. The cervical spine.
Why it matters: it lets your head nod, tilt and turn.

title: The Spine
question: How many bones are glowing?
lines: The low back carries the most weight. How many bones is it?
Watch the glowing section of the lower spine.
How many vertebrae are in the glowing section?
The neck has seven, and the rib-bearing mid-back has twelve.
The lumbar spine, in the low back, usually has five of the biggest.
It's C. Five.
Why it matters: big vertebrae carry much of your upper body's weight.

title: The Spine
question: Which section of the spine is it?
lines: Twelve vertebrae in your spine each carry a pair of ribs.
Watch the glowing section in the middle of the back.
Which section of the spine is it?
The lumbar section is lower and has bigger bones.
The glowing section is the upper and middle back.
It's D. The thoracic spine.
Why it matters: it forms the back of the rib cage.

title: The Spine
question: What are the top two vertebrae?
lines: Nod yes, then shake no. Two special bones just moved.
Watch the two small glowing bones at the top of the spine.
What are the top two vertebrae?
The sacrum and coccyx are at the very bottom.
Atlas is C1 and holds up the head. Axis is C2.
It's A. Atlas and axis.
Why it matters: together they let your head nod and turn.

title: The Spine
question: How many vertebrae form the sacrum?
lines: One bone at the base of your spine was once separate pieces.
Watch the glowing triangle at the bottom of the spine.
How many vertebrae form the sacrum?
The neck has seven vertebrae, but they stay separate.
The sacrum forms from five vertebrae that fuse together.
It's A. Five.
Why it matters: the sacrum forms the back wall of the pelvis.

title: The Spine
question: Which vertebrae connect to the ribs?
lines: Some of your vertebrae have ribs attached.
Watch the glowing vertebrae in the middle of the back.
Which vertebrae connect to the ribs?
Cervical vertebrae are in the neck and have no ribs attached.
Twelve ribs join the glowing vertebrae.
It's B. The thoracic vertebrae.
Why it matters: this link forms the back of the cage protecting the lungs.

title: The Spine
question: How many neck vertebrae are there?
lines: Even a giraffe has the same number of neck bones as you.
Watch the glowing bones of the neck.
How many neck vertebrae are there?
Twelve is the number of thoracic vertebrae, in the chest.
Counting from C1 to C7 gives the answer.
It's D. Seven.
Why it matters: this many small bones make your neck flexible.

title: The Spine
question: Which spine bone joins the pelvis?
lines: One bone of the spine locks into your hips. Name it.
Watch the glowing wedge at the bottom of the spine.
Which spine bone joins the pelvis?
The coccyx hangs below it, at the very end.
The glowing wedge sits between the two hip bones.
It's B. The sacrum.
Why it matters: it passes your body weight from the spine to the legs.

title: The Spine
question: Which spine section is the lower back?
lines: You use this part of your spine every time you bend over.
Watch the glowing section of the spine.
Which spine section is the lower back?
The thoracic section is higher, and its bones carry the ribs.
These five large vertebrae sit between the ribs and the pelvis.
It's C. The lumbar spine.
Why it matters: these big vertebrae carry much of your body weight.

title: The Spine
question: Which bones are fused vertebrae?
lines: Some spine bones start as separate vertebrae, then fuse together.
Watch the glowing bones at the bottom of the spine.
Which bones are fused vertebrae?
The lumbar vertebrae stay separate and movable.
These two bones at the base of the spine are fused vertebrae.
It's A. The sacrum and the coccyx.
Why it matters: fusing makes the base of the spine strong and stable.

title: The Spine
question: Which vertebra is the neck-base bump?
lines: Tilt your head forward. Feel the bump at the base of your neck.
Watch the glowing vertebra at the bottom of the neck.
Which vertebra makes that bump?
C1 is the top vertebra, right under the skull.
Its long spike points back under your skin.
It's C. C7.
Why it matters: doctors and students use it to count other vertebrae.

title: The Spine
question: How many vertebrae are not fused?
lines: The spine has a few fused bones and many that move.
Watch every glowing vertebra from the neck to the lower back.
How many separate vertebrae are glowing?
Thirty-three counts the fused sacrum and tailbone too.
Seven neck, twelve chest and five lower back.
It's A. Twenty-four.
Why it matters: these separate bones give the spine its movement.

title: The Spine
question: Which vertebra has the tooth-like peg?
lines: You shake your head no by turning on one small peg.
Watch the glowing second bone of the neck.
Which vertebra has the tooth-like peg?
The atlas is above it. It turns around the peg, it doesn't have one.
The peg is called the dens, and the atlas rotates on it.
It's B. The axis, C2.
Why it matters: most head turning to each side happens at this joint.
